title: A polynomial ideal with maximal contraction has a monic generator modulo that contraction
statement: Let R be a commutative ring, p an ideal of the polynomial ring R[T] [def-weil-polynomial-ring], and q its contraction along the coefficient map. If q is maximal and p is not qR[T], then there is a monic polynomial f with p = qR[T] + (f).

source.place: Tag 03C3, first proof paragraph, monic polynomial lift; exact formal generalization in Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/MonicSpan.lean:35

proof.text: Pass to (R/q)[T]. Since q is maximal, R/q is a field. The image of p is a nonzero ideal, hence has a monic generator g by polynomial division over a field. Lift g through the surjective coefficient quotient map to a monic polynomial f of the same degree. Taking inverse images of the principal ideal (g) gives p = qR[T] + (f). These steps are formalized by Polynomial.exists_monic_span_sup_map_eq, whose source and exact type were read in the pinned Mathlib.
